38.0.0.en: Engraver: engraving the precious stones and setting them.

38.0.1.en: Embroiderer: decorating cloth with gold threads by working them into the fabric.

38.0.2.en: Embroidery: the various works of embroidery in cloth.

38.0.3.en: He mentions the metals used in the tent under the leadership of Ithamar the priest, the youngest son of Aaron, and with the help of Bezaleel and Aholiab, who were skilled in the various crafts.

38.1.2.en: This is the quantity of gold used, and it is very great and equals millions of Egyptian pounds.

38.2.0.en: Talent: 3000 shekels, and the shekel of silver = 15 g.

38.2.1.en: The shekel of the sanctuary: an exact shekel kept in the house of the Lord to measure by.

38.2.2.en: "A bekah for every man": sometimes it is said half and at other times half a shekel, and the former is a kind of abbreviation.

38.2.3.en: He mentions here the quantity of silver used in the tent. Moses had collected the silver of the ransom for the males of the children of Israel before the tent of meeting was set up, and after the tent was set up a census was made of the number of males twenty years old and upward, and it was found that the amount of silver matched the number of males in the census (Num 1:46, 2:32, 33), and this shows the faithfulness of all the people in offering the silver of the ransom according to God's commands. There is another opinion that Moses also took a census before the tent was set up and collected the silver of the ransom.

38.3.0.en: He mentions here the quantity of bronze used in the tent.

38.3.1.en: The concern of the people to give for setting up the dwelling of God among them appears here, to call us to care for the churches and everything in them, for they are the greatest place in the world, where God dwells with His most holy Body and Blood.

39.0.0.en: "They did beat": they hammered the gold until it became very thin plates, and by heating they were able to turn them into threads.

39.1.s.en: (4) The glory of the Lord fills the tabernacle

39.1.0.en: After the tent was set up and anointed, the pillar of cloud came down on the tent and covered it, proclaiming God's blessing and His acceptance to dwell in their midst.

39.2.0.en: Moses was afraid to enter the tent, the dwelling of God, because of His glory and greatness. After a while God allowed them to enter and serve in it by renewing the oil of the lampstand and the showbread and offering the sacrifices on the bronze altar.

39.3.0.en: When the cloud rose in the sky and moved, the children of Israel journeyed after it, and when it came down they pitched the tent of meeting and their tents around it.

39.4.0.en: At night the pillar of cloud turned into a pillar of fire before the tent of meeting to give them light.

39.4.1.en: This pillar was a proclamation of the presence of God in their midst, in addition to its being their leader in their journeys as the Lord commanded, and this pillar was mentioned in detail in (ch. 13:21, 22).

39.4.2.en: How beautiful it is for God to lead your life, so that you move if He commands you to, and stand if He wishes, and this is by submission to the Church, the Holy Bible and the guidance of the father of confession.

39.4.3.en: Symbols of the tent of meeting. No. / The symbol / What is symbolized. 1. The tent of meeting in the midst of the camp: Christ incarnate in the midst of His people (Mt 1:23), and the Church or the Kingdom of Heaven (Heb 9:9, 23, 8:5). 2. Gold: divinity and glory. 3. Silver: redemption, because it was collected as a ransom for the males (ch. 30:12, 13), and it also refers to the word of God.

39.4.4.en: 4. Bronze: judgment, since the altar of burnt offering is made of it, with which God the Judge is pleased with His people.

39.4.5.en: 5. Acacia wood: the humanity of Christ, overlaid with gold because of the union of divinity with humanity in Christ. 6. Fine twined linen, that is, linen: the righteousness of Christ, which He gives to His believing children. 7. The color blue: heaven and the heavenly life. 8. The color purple: the kingship of Christ. 9. The color scarlet: the sufferings of Christ and His blood. 10. The hanging at the door of the tent: Christ is the door and the way (Jn 10:9, 14:6). And the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies. 11. The bronze altar of burnt offering: the crucified Christ, who is the way to the Holy of Holies.

39.4.6.en: 12. The laver: Baptism. 13. The boards of the tent overlaid with gold: the believers built up as living stones (1 Pet 2:5), covered by the glory of God. 14. The bars: unity (Eph 4:3). 15. The silver bases of the boards: the redemption on which the Church rests. 16. The colored linen covering of the tabernacle: the beauty of Christ and His virtues that appear in the colors, and His righteousness, which the linen signifies, and on it the Cherubim, that is, the angels who serve Him, and it also signifies the believer adorned with virtues, clothed with righteousness, for whom the angels intercede.

39.4.7.en: No. / The symbol / What is symbolized. 17. The covering of rams' skins dyed red: the blood of Christ the Redeemer. 18. The covering of goats' hair: the sacrifice of Christ, whom the goats that are slain signify. 19. The covering of badgers' skins: Christ, the Church and the believer, who shows outward weakness but in whom is the power of God. 20. The altar of incense: Christ the Intercessor, who died, that is, was burned, for us. 21. The golden lampstand: the Holy Spirit, who works in Christ and works in the Church and the believers. 22. The table of showbread: the incarnate Christ, who gives us His Body and Blood on the altar. 23. The veil between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies: sin and enmity, which separate God and man, and which Christ removed by His redemption (the tearing of the veil at the death of Christ). 24. The Holy of Holies: heaven, where the throne of God is and where He dwells in His glory, and it is a cube, so it signifies the Holy Trinity.

39.4.8.en: 25. The ark of the covenant: the presence of God in the midst of His people, and the incarnate Christ, and the Virgin who carried divinity in her womb.

39.4.9.en: 26. The cover: the mercy of God, because the blood is sprinkled on it, so that divine justice, represented in the Cherubim, is satisfied, and it also points to the Virgin, who is overshadowed by the angels.

39.4.10.en: 27. The two tablets of the Law inside the ark: Christ the Word of God. 28. The pot of manna inside the ark: the manna signifies the incarnate Christ and the Body and Blood of Christ, and the Virgin Mary, whom the pot signifies.

39.4.11.en: 29. Aaron's rod that budded: Christ who rose, and the Virgin Mary, who gave birth without seed. The ark: man.
